title: Write the investment committee memo
summary: Turn the underwriting into a decision document: the thesis, sourced facts, sources and uses, the returns and what drives them, the debt tests, scenarios, risks, open items and a recommendation with its conditions. The people the governing documents name then approve it in writing.

steps.title: Freeze the model and list where each figure came from
steps.instruction: Save a dated copy of the underwriting model the memo will present and give it a version number; every figure in the memo comes from that version. Build a source table: each property fact, market fact, rent, expense, loan term and assumption, with the document and page it came from, such as the rent roll, a lease abstract, the trailing-12, the tax record, the comp set, the site visit report or the term sheet. Mark each figure verified, seller-reported or assumed. A figure with no source goes on a gap list; it is never filled with an estimate that looks like a fact. In Texas, appraisal districts appraise at market value as of January 1; for years after the purchase, source the tax line from purchase price evidence and each taxing unit's rate in the property-tax calculator, not the seller's bill, and keep the closing year on the roll value.
steps.modeBasis: Versioning a file and tracing each figure to a document is file work an agent can do.

steps.title: Write the thesis and the business plan
steps.instruction: Write the thesis in one paragraph: what is being bought, at what price, why it is worth more to the sponsor than that price, and the two or three things that must be true for that to hold. Name the strategy, such as stable income, lease-up, renovation or repositioning, and the hold it implies; where the case rests on one tenant, tie the hold to that tenant's remaining term. Then set out the business plan year by year: leasing, capital work, management changes and the planned refinance or sale, each with its cost and who does it. State year-one cash flow after debt service; if the deal pays little or nothing until the sale, say so in the thesis.
steps.modeBasis: The thesis and plan are written from the approved model and the deal file; the judgment they express belongs to a person who signs as author.

typeNotes.industrial: For a single-tenant building, say why the tenant's operation is hard or easy to move: equipment, power, permits, labor or customers nearby. A tenant that could leave easily makes the lease the whole case.
typeNotes.multifamily: State how many units are renovated each year, the cost per unit, and the rent premium the comp set supports.

steps.title: Describe the property and the market, with sources
steps.instruction: Describe the property from the source table: site, buildings, age, construction, occupancy, each tenant with its credit and remaining term, and the condition the site visit found. Judge the income by its amount, its quality and how long it lasts: compare the remaining lease terms with the loan term and the hold. Then the market: the submarket's occupancy against its own longer-run level, space under construction, recent absorption, and the rent and sale comps. Say where the submarket sits in its cycle and what that means for the rent growth and exit cap assumed. Cite the source row for every fact, and list each place the underwriting departs from the offering memorandum, with the reason.
steps.modeBasis: Every fact comes from documents and data already in the deal file; an agent writes and cites them.

typeNotes.industrial: Compare clear height, dock doors, truck court, power, site coverage and outside storage with the comps; these decide who else could use the building.
typeNotes.multifamily: Show the unit mix, in-place rents against the comps, concessions and delinquency.
typeNotes.office: Show rollover by year, allowances and leasing commissions still owed, and parking.
typeNotes.retail: Show the anchors and their terms, tenant sales where reported, and any co-tenancy or exclusive-use clauses.

steps.title: Lay out sources and uses and the loan terms
steps.instruction: List the uses: price, closing costs, loan fees and lender reserves, capital work funded at closing, any acquisition fee and working capital. List the sources: the senior loan and equity by holder, such as the sponsor, investors or the capital partner. Sources must equal uses to the dollar. Show the price per square foot or unit and the going-in cap rate on in-place and on underwritten net operating income. From the term sheet, state the loan amount, fixed or floating rate with index and spread, term, amortization, any interest-only period, prepayment terms, recourse and guaranties, reserves and covenants, and which sizing limit binds. Show the balance due at maturity, and for a floating rate, the payment along the rate path and any rate cap.
steps.modeBasis: The figures come from the model and the term sheet, and the calculators do the arithmetic.

steps.title: Show the returns and what drives them
steps.instruction: State the hurdle first and how it was set: a dated risk-free reference, such as the Treasury yield for a term like the hold, plus a premium for this property's risk, or the buy box target. Then report unlevered and levered IRR, equity multiple, cash-on-cash by year and net present value at the hurdle. Run the npv-irr calculator to show how much of the value comes from operations and how much from the sale; a large sale share means the case rests on the exit cap, so put the exit cap beside the going-in cap and explain any gap. If the equity cash flows change sign more than once, the IRR may not be unique: say so and lean on NPV. Rank any options by NPV at the hurdle. Show investor returns after the promote.
steps.modeBasis: The calculators are live and run from the frozen model's cash flows; the hurdle is a stated input.

steps.title: Test the leverage and the break-evens
steps.instruction: Run the leverage calculator. Compare the going-in cap rate with the loan constant: when the constant is higher, added debt lowers the cash return on equity. Show cash-on-cash at a few loan-to-value levels and, if two quotes differ in size, what the extra loan dollars cost against the unlevered return. Report break-even occupancy, the interest rate at which the loan payment equals net operating income, and coverage after the largest tenant leaves. At maturity, test the exit-year income against the coverage and debt yield a refinancing lender might apply, marking those limits as assumptions. Put each loan covenant beside the downside case.
steps.modeBasis: The tests are arithmetic on the model and the term sheet, run in live calculators.

steps.title: Run sensitivities and weighted scenarios
steps.instruction: Read the returns-sensitivity table for exit cap and growth, then move the one or two inputs this deal turns on, such as renewal odds, downtime, capital cost or the interest rate, one at a time. Next build at least three full cases, downside, base and upside, each with its own net operating income, value, IRR, coverage and loan-to-value. Give each case a weight, state that the weights are judgment, and run the scenario-risk calculator for the expected return, standard deviation and coefficient of variation. A handful of cases understates the tails, so describe the worst case in words as well. Hand the downside figures to the risk section.
steps.modeBasis: Cases are model runs from stated inputs; the weights are a person's judgment, recorded as such.

typeNotes.industrial: Make the downside the single tenant leaving at expiration: the building empty for the downtime, re-leased at market rent with leasing costs, and coverage while it is empty. A general vacancy line does not cover losing the only tenant. State the dollars needed to carry the building empty and re-lease it in this downside (debt service, taxes, insurance, upkeep and leasing costs over the downtime), the reserve raised at closing, and where any more would come from under the governing agreement.
typeNotes.multifamily: Move rent growth, concessions and turnover cost; one unit going dark matters little, a market rent drop matters a lot.
typeNotes.office: Model the largest expirations rolling with downtime, allowances and commissions at market.
typeNotes.retail: Model an anchor leaving and what the co-tenancy clauses then let other tenants do.

steps.title: Show the after-tax view for taxable investors
steps.instruction: Where the investors are taxable, show before-tax and after-tax IRR side by side with the after-tax calculator, every rate entered as an input and stated in the memo. Under the general depreciation system, buildings are depreciated by the straight line method, residential rental property over 27.5 years and nonresidential real property over 39 years; land is not depreciated, so state the land and building split used. On a sale, the part of an individual's long-term gain that reflects depreciation is unrecaptured section 1250 gain, taxed at a maximum 25 percent rate, and individuals may also owe the 3.8 percent net investment income tax. Label the result arithmetic on stated inputs, not tax advice, and have the CPA confirm the assumptions, such as passive loss limits, before it circulates.
steps.modeBasis: The arithmetic runs on stated rates in a live calculator; the tax assumptions are the CPA's to confirm.

steps.title: Set out the risks by kind and what answers each
steps.instruction: List the risks by kind: income and vacancy, tenant credit and concentration, exit value and how quickly the property could sell, execution and management, interest rate and refinancing, expense inflation, legislative and regulatory, such as zoning, permits and the property tax line after a sale, environmental, flood and physical condition, and the financial risk of the leverage and its covenants. For each, give its effect on the numbers from the sensitivities and scenarios, and say how it is answered: priced into the offer or reserves, reduced by insurance, a rate cap, lease terms or contract protections, checked in due diligence, or accepted. Separate what the sponsor controls from what it can only price. Never list a risk without its effect and its answer.
steps.modeBasis: The risk list is written from the model runs and the deal file; accepting a risk is the approvers' call.

steps.title: List open items and draft the recommendation
steps.instruction: List every item not yet verified, such as estoppels, the Phase I, the condition report, the survey, the appraisal, zoning and title, with what it could change, the step that answers it and the date it must be settled by. Then draft the recommendation: proceed, proceed on conditions, or pass. If proceeding, state the maximum price, the terms that matter most to it, and the conditions, such as diligence results that must hold, financing terms, the most equity the deal may take and any consents. Name the findings that would send the deal back to the approvers, with the threshold the approvers set for each. Recommend a pass when the downside outweighs the expected reward.
steps.modeBasis: The draft is writing from the file; the recommendation is a proposal the approvers accept, change or reject.

steps.title: Tie out the figures and control who sees the memo
steps.instruction: Check every figure in the memo against the frozen model version and the source table, and re-run the calculators if the model changed while drafting. Remove figures left from earlier drafts. Mark the memo internal. If the memo, an excerpt or its figures will go to investors, federal law makes it unlawful, in connection with buying or selling a security, to make an untrue statement of a material fact or omit one needed to keep the statements from misleading. For a fund that would be an investment company but for section 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7), an Advisers Act rule bars its investment adviser from the same toward investors and prospective investors. For a joint venture, counsel says whether the interest is a security. Counsel reviews anything investors will see.
steps.modeBasis: Matching figures to the model is document control; whether and how anything goes to investors is approved by a person, with counsel.

steps.title: Take the memo to the fund's investment committee
steps.instruction: Circulate the memo, the model and the source table to the investment committee the fund agreement establishes, with the notice it requires. Hold the vote with the quorum and majority the agreement sets, and have a member with a conflict step out where it says so. Record the decision, the approved maximum price and every condition in writing, by signed minutes or a written consent as the agreement allows, and fill the memo's decision and approver fields. If the deal also needs advisory committee or investor consent, for example for a purchase from a related party or an exception to a limit, get it before a letter of intent commits the fund. Then hand the approved terms to the letter of intent.
steps.modeBasis: Committee members vote under the fund agreement; an agent circulates the materials and records the result.

steps.title: Get the capital partner's written approval
steps.instruction: Send the capital partner the memo, the model and the source table under the approval right the JV agreement or term sheet gives it, and ask for its decision by a stated date. Answer its questions from the source table, put any changed assumption into a new model version, and re-run the affected calculators so the memo and the model stay matched. Get the approval in writing, with its conditions, in the form the agreement requires, and fill the memo's decision and approver fields. Do not send a letter of intent or sign anything the partner must approve before that approval arrives.
steps.modeBasis: The approval is the capital partner's own decision under its agreement; an agent prepares and tracks the materials.

steps.title: Have the sponsor's principals approve in writing
steps.instruction: In a syndication the sponsor's principals decide. Circulate the memo to the principals the sponsor's company agreement or partner agreement names for investment decisions, and decide by the vote or consent it requires. Record the decision, the approved maximum price and the conditions in a written consent each required principal signs or confirms, and fill the memo's decision and approver fields. Where the agreement is silent, the principals agree in writing how this decision is made before they make it. The approved memo, not a draft, is the basis for the letter of intent and for the projections the offering shows.
steps.modeBasis: An investment decision binds the sponsor and is made by its principals; an agent circulates the memo and records the consent.
